expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint, not a full rewrite
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses the bug ('The classic bug: parent doesn't close p[0] and p[1] after forking... wc blocks on read, never gets EOF') and gives a minimal fix — placement of close() calls in the existing ~20-line pipe/fork/dup2 pattern, the current milestone only, not a multi-milestone implementation

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a runnable check: 'while it hangs, run `lsof -c wc` in another terminal — you'll see an extra pipe fd held by the parent (or a child), which is your leak' — concrete command plus expected observation

expectations.text: B3: Identifies that the parent (and/or children) must close unused pipe file descriptors, otherwise wc never sees EOF
expectations.evidence: 'EOF on a pipe is only delivered when ALL write-end descriptors are closed. The parent's p[1] (and any child that kept it) keeps the pipe open, so wc's read() blocks forever'; 'the parent must close BOTH pipe fds immediately after both forks' and 'both children must close both raw fds after dup2'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)', 'SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; only read-only grep/glob tool calls inside the workspace; no install commands and nothing written outside the project
